floating_group_geometry.physical_position: Between the three-part header and the first main-grid ciphertext row.
floating_group_geometry.literal_stream_order: Physical top-to-bottom order: floating group first, then the main grid with its blank cell skipped. This literal order is retained separately from the modeled third-group placement.

main_grid_blank_cell.interpretation: Blank layout cell, not an inserted erasure in the literal stream.

notes: The group FGFFF is physically above the main grid. Literal top-to-bottom reading includes it first. The declared model moves those same five observed coordinates to the third-group position, after 10 main-grid coordinates; no source letter is discarded or invented.
The source announces three parts and labels this one 1 TL, but parts 2 and 3 are not printed beneath it.

The proposed association with p192 parts 2 and 3 is based on their combined forwarding/address/appointment syntax and matching key, not pagination adjacency. The p199 November 15 header conflicts with the p192 November 14 page heading; both remain literal.

historical_reference.identity_limit: Matching the encrypted surname to this historical person is a separate inference, not an already established plaintext or an observed original appointment telegram.

scope_notes: The displayed p192 begins with unheaded parts 2 and 3. A separately sourced p199 part 1 supplies a strongly matching forwarding preamble; their cross-page association and conflicting date headings remain explicit.
The damaged part 3 has exactly 227 valid source letters against RICHI-232. The stated model restores one missing five-coordinate group.
The geometry stencil excludes the entire eight-letter courier name and seven-letter signature. Historical TYDELSKI is used only after the gap search.

cross_page_association.status: Strong textual association; not an established matching source header for the unheaded parts.
source_evidence: p199 unlettered message declares 3 TLE and provides 1 TL only.
p192 provides unheaded 2 TL and 3 TL without a surviving message header on that page.
p199 1 TL asks General von Kress in Tiflis to forward a Polish Foreign Ministry telegram to WACLAW V OSTROWSKI.
p192 2 TL begins TIFLISDOPPELPUNKT and the appointment text; part 3 completes the appointment and says instructions have already been sent through a courier.
All three records decrypt under the unchanged Nov13-15b published key.
cross_page_association.date_caveat: The p199 header explicitly says November 15 / 15/11. The p192 page is headed November 14. The separate p192 A and B headers also pair November 14 receipt dates with 15/11 originating dates; these inconsistencies are preserved, not resolved here.
cross_page_association.historical_context: The independent Mądzik archival study discusses Wacław Ostrowski as a Polish representative in Tbilisi in 1918 (printed pp. 78–79). This is corroboration after the source reading, not a crib used to select the floating-group position.
